ArtifactDate: Ptolemaic–Byzantine periods (archive; 1st–6th centuries AD for the biblical papyri)
Description: The vast papyrus archive recovered from the rubbish mounds of Oxyrhynchus by Bernard Grenfell and Arthur Hunt: hundreds of thousands of fragments covering tax receipts, private letters, and literature — including some of the earliest surviving New Testament papyri. This entry covers the archive itself; individual papyri already listed elsewhere are distinct entries and are not repeated here.
BiblicalSignificance: Oxyrhynchus is how we know ordinary Christians owned, copied, and carried the Scriptures within a generation or two of the apostles. A rubbish mound preserved what persecution and time could not erase: the everyday paperwork of a church that wrote its faith down.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the archive is the Oxyrhynchus rubbish-mound deposit; individual fragments are dated and identified case by case, and the archive as a whole illuminates early Christian book culture rather than any single passage.
